extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news organizations, and the general public interested in journalism awards and exemplary reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Press release announcing the 2024 George Polk Awards and describing the qualities, categories, and examples of work that the awards recognize; includes stipulations for the separate Sydney Schanberg Prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative and enterprising reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The George Polk Awards 'place a premium on investigative and enterprising reporting that gains attention and achieves results.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded annually to honor special achievement in journalism; emphasis on reporting that is investigative, enterprising, attracts public attention, and produces tangible outcomes or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners were selected from submissions 'of work that appeared in print, online or on television or radio, nominated by news organizations and individuals or recommended by a panel of former winners.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in any of these media formats may be submitted; nominations may come from news organizations, individuals, or recommendations by a panel of former winners. (Example: 493 submissions considered for 2024 awards.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact / produces results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting that 'gains attention and achieves results' — stories that lead to changes, policy pauses, institutional reforms, or platform-safety updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: reporting that led the UAE to pause some operations in Sudan; Roblox rolling out safety updates; Meta removing 70,000 accounts; a medical school ending the challenged practice; practices being curtailed after exposure. Impact on policy, corporate behavior, or institutional practice is a key evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting under personal risk or in conflict zones
rubrics_metrics.description: Work 'reported at great personal risk' and on-the-ground reporting from war zones and deeply unsafe contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: dispatches from Sudan that documented starvation and atrocities; reporting on the invasion of Ukraine while keeping sources and the reporter safe. Courage, willingness to report in dangerous environments, and sourcing under risk are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data and records to establish facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Dogged use of data, public records, hospital records, and death certificates to establish facts and reveal systemic problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Baltimore Banner's data-driven work documenting overdose crisis; ProPublica's mining of hospital records and death certificates to reveal preventable deaths. Emphasis on rigorous data collection/analysis and document-based reporting, often done despite official resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence and overcoming resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists exhibit persistence — multi-part investigations, multi-year research, and work undertaken 'in the face of city officials' resistance' or other obstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: five years of research leading to Justice Reporting revelations; Local Reporting accomplished despite official resistance; long-term reporting that 'results from staying with a story, sometimes at great risk or sacrifice.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and long-form treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: In-depth, long-form reporting and multi-part series are prized (examples include six-part series and single pieces of 20,000+ and 35,000 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Schanberg Prize explicitly requires at least 5,000 words; winners cited include 20,000-word and 35,000-word works. Multi-part series (e.g., six-part) and sustained narrative depth are highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposing systemic corporate, governmental, or institutional wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting that uncovers systemic abuses, corrupt practices, or institutional failures that harm the public, patients, or communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: exposés of UnitedHealth Group's massive reach and profit-driven harms; bird-flu response delayed by political considerations; secret police deals to hide corruption; financial mismanagement and misconduct in public figures leading to Senate scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-protection and fraud exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations exposing scams, consumer deception, and concrete financial or physical harms to vulnerable populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: San Antonio Express-News series on door-to-door solar contractors training scam artists who targeted elderly homeowners, leaving them with useless systems and damaged roofs. Concrete evidence of consumer harm and misleading practices is central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncovering abuses with human-centered narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative-driven pieces that center human experiences, often revealing betrayal, trauma, or systemic injustice through detailed profiles or long-form storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: magazine piece 'Alice Munro's Passive Voice' (20,000-word) delving into a novelist's reaction to abuse; podcast 'The Parole Room' following repeated parole efforts and systemic barriers. Emphasis on storytelling that illuminates broader systemic issues via individual experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast and television investigative reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Television reporting that documents institutional abuses, uses detailed findings, and prompts institutional response or policy change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: National Television Reporting that revealed a medical school dismembering corpses, led to the school ending the practice after reporters shared detailed findings. High standards of documentation and storytelling for visual/broadcast media are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of sources and reporter safety in hostile environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting that protects sources and keeps reporting teams safe when operating under threat or security surveillance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reporter who 'kept herself and her sources safe from Russian security services' while producing long-form coverage of deserters. Ethical/safety practices and operational security are evaluative considerations in dangerous reporting contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology and platform-harm reporting that leads to platform changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative work exposing online child safety risks, sextortion, and illicit sales that results in platform or industry responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Technology Reporting that revealed abuses on Roblox, Instagram, and Snapchat and led to Roblox safety updates and Meta removing accounts. Emphasis on revealing digital harms and eliciting concrete platform action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term research and demonstrable policy consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained investigative efforts (multi-year research) that uncover practices and lead to curtailment or reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Justice Reporting that was 'a product of five years of research' detailing how police arranged secret deals; the practice was curtailed after publication. Longitudinal research and demonstrable policy or practice changes are rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sydney Schanberg Prize explicit criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schanberg Prize 'honor[s] long-form investigative or enterprise journalism embodying qualities reflected in [Jane Freiman Schanberg's] late husband's legendary career' and was established to honor 'highly distinguished, deep coverage of armed conflicts; local, state or federal government corruption; military injustice; war crimes, genocide or sedition; or authoritarian government abuses' of at least 5,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize comes with a $25,000 award funded by Freiman Schanberg; editorial emphasis on highly distinguished, deep coverage of armed conflict or government/military abuses, minimum length threshold (≥5,000 words), and staying with a story often at personal risk or sacrifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-based judging
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards are conferred across specified categories (e.g., Foreign Reporting, War Reporting, National Reporting, Local Reporting, State Reporting, Health Care Reporting, Medical Reporting, Political Reporting, Justice Reporting, Technology Reporting, Magazine Reporting, National Television Reporting, Foreign Television Reporting, Podcast, Sydney Schanberg Prize).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work is evaluated and selected within these category frameworks; the category defines topical focus and relevant evaluative expectations (e.g., War Reporting values front-line dispatches; Medical Reporting values record-based uncovering of medical harm).
